content: 1. Voriconazole should be used immediately after reconstitution. 2. Calculate the required amount of Vfend (voriconazole), withdraw it, and discard an equivalent volume from the infusion bag or bottle. 3. Add the voriconazole solution to the infusion bag or bottle. 4. The final infusion concentration should not exceed 5 mg/mL. 5. Administer the intravenous infusion over 1 to 2 hours, ensuring the infusion rate does not exceed 3 mg/kg/hour. 6. Do not mix voriconazole with other drugs, parenteral nutrition, or sodium bicarbonate in the same infusion. 7. Store the vials at a temperature between 15°C and 30°C (59°F to 86°F). 8. Voriconazole, marketed under the brand name Vfend, is an antifungal medication used to treat a variety of fungal infections. 9. It belongs to the azole class of antifungal drugs. 10. Before starting voriconazole, read the patient information leaflet provided by your pharmacist. 11. The dosage and duration of treatment depend on your medical condition, weight, response to treatment, and any other medications you may be taking. 12. For optimal results, take voriconazole at evenly spaced intervals. 13. Continue taking the medication for the full prescribed duration, even if symptoms improve after a few days. 14. Common side effects include nausea, vomiting, and headache. 15. This medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. 16. Rarely, voriconazole can cause severe, potentially fatal liver disease. 17. Serious allergic reactions to voriconazole are rare, but mild rashes are common and usually not serious. 18. However, it may be difficult to distinguish a mild rash from a rare, severe allergic reaction. 19. Voriconazole may cause QT prolongation, a condition that affects heart rhythm. 20. The risk of QT prolongation increases if you have certain medical conditions or are taking other medications that can cause QT prolongation. 21. Low potassium or magnesium levels in the blood can also increase the risk of QT prolongation. 22. This risk may be heightened by the use of diuretics or conditions such as severe sweating, diarrhea, or vomiting. 23. Voriconazole may cause vision changes. 24. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or performing tasks requiring clear vision until you are confident you can do so safely. 25. This medication can increase sensitivity to sunlight and may elevate the risk of skin cancer, especially with prolonged use. 26. Limit sun exposure, avoid tanning booths and sunlamps, and use sunscreen and protective clothing when outdoors. 27. Inform your doctor if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. 28. Avoid becoming pregnant while using voriconazole, as it may harm an unborn baby. 29. Discuss reliable birth control options with your doctor while taking this medication. 30. It is unknown if voriconazole passes into breast milk, but breastfeeding is not recommended due to potential risks to the infant. 31. Drug interactions may alter how voriconazole or other medications work, or increase the risk of serious side effects. 32. Keep a list of all medications and supplements you use and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. 33. Voriconazole can slow the removal of other medications from your body, potentially affecting their efficacy. 34. Similarly, other medications can affect how voriconazole is metabolized, altering its effectiveness. 35. Examples of interacting drugs include butalbital, efavirenz, mitotane, rifamycins (e.g., rifabutin, rifampin), ritonavir, secobarbital, and certain seizure medications (e.g., carbamazepine, phenobarbital). 36. In case of overdose with serious symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call emergency services (911 in the U.S.) immediately. 37. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. 38. This medication is prescribed for your current condition only. 39. Laboratory and medical tests (e.g., liver and kidney function, blood mineral levels) should be conducted before and during treatment with voriconazole. 40. Attend all scheduled medical and laboratory appointments. 41. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. 42. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. 43. Store voriconazole at room temperature, away from light and moisture. 44. Do not store it in the bathroom. 45. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. 46. Properly discard expired or unused medication. 47. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about voriconazole. 48. It does not guarantee that the medication is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. 49. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this medication and your specific health needs.
